question: What is Angular change detection?
shortAnswer: The process that syncs component state to the DOM by checking bindings when the app may have changed.
detailedAnswer: Traditionally Zone.js patches async APIs and triggers CD. Default strategy checks the whole tree; OnPush checks when inputs/events/signals mark the view dirty.

question: How does ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush improve performance?
shortAnswer: OnPush skips checking a subtree unless inputs change by reference, events fire, or the view is marked dirty.
detailedAnswer: Combine with immutable inputs and async pipe/signals. Mutating objects in place without marking dirty won't update the view.

question: What does markForCheck vs detectChanges do?
shortAnswer: markForCheck marks the path to root dirty for the next CD; detectChanges runs CD immediately on that view.
detailedAnswer: Use markForCheck inside OnPush when updating state outside Angular's knowledge. detectChanges is sharper and can be used carefully in tests/directives.

question: Why can mutating an @Input object fail to update an OnPush child?
shortAnswer: OnPush compares input references; in-place mutation keeps the same reference.
detailedAnswer: Clone/update immutably or call markForCheck. Prefer signals which notify dependents on set.

question: How do signals interact with change detection?
shortAnswer: Updating a signal marks dependent views dirty so Angular can refresh only what needs updating.
detailedAnswer: Signal-based CD reduces reliance on Zone.js. computed/effect form a reactive graph. Templates reading signals establish dependencies.

question: When would you detach a change detector?
shortAnswer: Rare cases like high-frequency updates where you manually control when to reattach/detect.
detailedAnswer: Detaching skips automatic checks. Easy to forget reattach—prefer OnPush/signals first. Useful for virtual scroll internals sometimes.
